verdict.rationale: Airbyte's docs explicitly define incremental sync as pulling 'only the data that has changed since the previous sync' (airbyte-docs-22), backed by sync-mode concepts (airbyte-docs-7/23) and CDC log-based replication that tracks position and captures INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE changes without full reloads (airbyte-docs-15/25/38/42) — this is exactly cursor/state management handled automatically. Community reports corroborate real-world use for continuous incremental syncing (airbyte-comm-4/5), though one shows a workaround needed for an extremely large initial-load table before incremental syncing worked reliably. missing for 10: independent large-scale benchmarking of state/cursor reliability across all connector types, and confirmation that non-CDC sources handle hard deletes as cleanly as CDC ones (an older community complaint flagged this gap).
